subject: Modeling Heterogeneous Variance of Random Effects in brms

messages.author: 78e87438f257ed86
messages.subject: Modeling Heterogeneous Variance of Random Effects in brms
parts:
Hi Paul,

I recently started using the brms package, and I wanted to thank you for making it so easy to work with Stan from inside R. The package is simply phenomenal.

I'm working on a very specific problem in survey methodology, and I'm wondering how one might specify the models that I have in mind using the brm() function. In short, I study whether different groups of survey interviewers (treated as clusters in a two-level model) may vary in terms of the between-interviewer variance that they introduce in survey responses. For example, inexperienced interviewers may introduce more variability in survey responses than experienced interviewers. Considering random intercepts only, this would mean that the variance of the random interviewer intercepts is allowed to vary across different groups of interviewers.

I'm attaching a recent paper that describes this type of application. In the appendix, you can see SAS and WinBUGS code for fitting the model that I have in mind.

Thinking more generally (in a longitudinal context), males and females may vary in terms of the variance of their random intercepts or random slopes (or both).

I looked around online a lot to see if this had come up in the context of brms, and this was the closest post that I could find:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/brms-users/-L36FEehE68

I didn't quite understand your responses from last July, and whether this would result in fitting the model that I have in mind. In my context, there isn't necessarily a predictor (although one could also allow the mean responses to vary across the different groups of interviewers as well, via a fixed group effect); I just want to compare a model allowing for heterogeneous interviewer variance components with a model fixing that variance to be equal across interviewer groups.

If there was a way to fit this model using brm(), I would sincerely appreciate hearing your thoughts!

Thank you for your time and your contributions.

-Brady

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Modeling Heterogeneous Variance of Random Effects in brms
parts:
Hi Brady,

just to clarify the idea. We want to model not a single random effects SD across participants, but one SD for participants in the first group and another SD for participants in the other group, right?

I think that it is not yet possible with brms, mainly because it is not expressible in standard lme4 syntax (which brms extends). If you like, please open an issue on brms' github page for this so that I don't loose track of it and may implement it at some point.

Best,
Paul
